title: Micro-output telemetry, SLA anchors, and privacy guards for live responses
creator: Ivy Nguyen
description: Goal: instrument live token/fragment outputs with per-fragment latency, error and token-size metrics, correlate each fragment to a tracing span, and apply deterministic redaction rules before logs reach centralized pipelines. This enables SLA anchors (per-response tail latency targets), fast RCA for failed function calls, and PII minimization in observability.
acceptance_criteria: Each streamed fragment emitted by the runtime must produce a telemetry event containing: fragment_id, parent_request_id, timestamp, token_count, generation_latency_ms, model_variant, and a trace_span_id.
Telemetry events are sampled at two rates: high-frequency (1%) stored in full-index and low-frequency (100% aggregated) for rollup histograms
A tracing span is opened when the response starts and child spans are created per-fragment; spans must be linkable in the Trace UI with request-level context.
Redaction pipeline runs within the runtime before emitting logs; PII patterns (emails, SSNs, credit cards) are masked and a redaction_reason tag is added.
Console dashboard shows per-fragment P50/P95/P99 latencies and token throughput per model per customer.
No raw fragment content leaves the cluster unless dataset-level consent flag is set; tests demonstrate redaction failsafe in CI.
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Spike completed comparing two sampling strategies (uniform vs adaptive by error-rate). Adaptive performed better for error hotspots.
2026-02-25: Prototype telemetry envelope implemented in runtime; emits fragment_id and basic timing, backed by local log sink.
2026-03-02: Security review pre-check: identified regex performance issue for naive PII patterns — switched to compiled automaton.
2026-03-08: Integration test added to ensure trace_span_id propagates to function/tool-calls and is visible in Jaeger.
2026-03-11: Cross-team API review with Console and Runtime teams; agreed on rollup histograms schema and retention policy.
testing_plan: Unit tests for telemetry envelope serialization and size limits
Load test that emits 10k concurrent streaming requests and verifies sampling rates and histogram stability
Fuzz PII redactor with corpora from incident logs to validate masking coverage
E2E smoke verifying trace span linkage from runtime -> function-caller -> fallback route
qa_notes: Monitor rollout with a canary group (10 customers) and enable debug-level fragment logs for early diagnostics.
Ensure canary can be toggled at account level via feature flag; emergency kill-switch added to disable fragment content emission.
Coordinate with Legal on retention limits for sampled fragment traces.
deployment_plan: Deploy runtime artifact with telemetry toggles to staging and run full load tests.
Push console dashboard changes behind feature flag.
Enable canary for internal customers for 48 hours and review errors and cost impact.
Gradual ramp to 100% over 5 days if SLOs hold.
open_questions: What is the final sampling ratio for high-frequency raw fragments (1% vs 0.5%)? Need SRE input on storage cost tradeoffs.
Should redaction be lossy (replace with token count) or replace sensitive spans with deterministic placeholders?
Do we allow customer-controlled redaction exceptions for enterprise customers with signed agreements?
notes: Incident learnings: previous PII leak in logs occurred when early streamed traces included unredacted tool inputs — new pipeline must protect tool calls as well.
This ticket pairs with PM-712 (SLA target definitions) for defining per-route latency anchors.
